## Definition and typical features 
These studies use interviews, focus groups, or other qualitative methods to collect information from smaller samples of researchers and other interest-holders on methodological issues. Researchers apply qualitative methods such as qualitative content analysis or thematic analysis. Sampling strategies, including convenience, purposive, or random sampling, and data saturation are other important design features. 

- Strengths include the focus on participants and explanatory depth. 
- Key challenges include limited generalizability due to small sample sizes and the influence of the investigators. rs.

## Typical purposes and corresponding examples 
[Assess methodological practice](../purposes/4assess-practice.qmd): Interviews to understand the reasons for non-reporting of outcomes.[@Smyth2011frequency]

[Evaluate a single method](../purposes/7evaluate-method.qmd): Focus group addressing the clarity of plain language recommendations in guidelines;[@Santesso2022focus] Interviews to test the face validity of a quality assessment instrument.[@Schandelmaier2020development]

[Develop guidance for understanding and applying methods](../purposes/9guidance-applying.qmd): Q-methodology, focus groups, content analysis, and workshops to produce guidance on creating summaries for trial participants.[@Bruhn2022recap]

[Research the dissemination and implementation of methods](../purposes/13implementation.qmd): Interview of trial investigators to understand why they did not use existing core outcome sets?[@Hughes2022in-depth]
